memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not turn to mediums or seek out spiritists, for you will be defiled by them. I am the LORD your God.'" - Lev 19:31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God forbids seeking out mediums and spiritists — those who claim to contact the dead.

We should be careful how we handle this. Some of what passes for contacting the dead is fraud, exploiting grieving people for money. Scripture takes the underlying spiritual realm seriously, but it is not our business to speculate about mechanics. What God says plainly is: do not go there.

And behind the prohibition is compassion. Think about who seeks a medium. Almost always someone grieving — a widow, a bereaved parent, someone desperate for one more word from the person they lost.

God is not being harsh with the grieving. He is protecting them from being exploited, and from a search that leads away from the only real comfort.

Because Christianity has something better to say about the dead than any medium ever could. We do not want you to be uninformed about those who sleep in death, so that you do not grieve like the rest of mankind, who have no hope (1 Thess 4:13). Not "do not grieve" — grieve, but with hope.

Jesus stood outside a tomb and wept, and then called a dead man out (John 11:35, 43-44). He has the keys of death (Rev 1:18).

You do not need a medium. You need the risen Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you been tempted to seek comfort somewhere God has forbidden?
2. What does Christian hope offer the grieving that nothing else can?
3. Who do you know who is grieving and needs real hope?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when I grieve, keep me from looking for comfort where You have said not to go. Anchor me in the risen Christ, who holds the keys of death. Amen.
